pages.text: Warm light spreads everywhere. Sunny the desert wakes up under a big open sky.
Rain rarely visits Sunny. Deserts are very dry places with little water.
During the day, the sand feels hot. When night comes, the desert can turn cold.
Wind shapes the land. Sand moves slowly, forming hills called dunes.
Not much grows here, but some plants store water to survive the dry days.
Animals rest during the hottest hours. Many come out when the sun is low.
Camels walk across Sunny’s land. Wide feet help them move on soft sand.
Sometimes water appears in small spots called oases. Life gathers there.
Sunny reminds us: deserts look empty, but many living things call them home.
At bedtime, we remember: deserts are dry, shaped by wind, and full of quiet life.
